pamphlet_excerpts: Engine Shutdown Protocol: Turn off the boat motor completely before any skier approaches the boarding ladder.
Submerged Debris Survey: Scout shallow water zones and sandbars prior to towing skiers at high speeds.
Tow Line Clearance: Keep floating towlines away from rotating boat propellers to prevent sudden line entanglements.
Weather Awareness Standards: Cease all towing operations immediately whenever lightning strikes or dense fog develops offshore.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Course Reconnaissance: Survey the planned tow corridor for shallow sandbars, floating logs, and mooring buoys.
Step 2 - Crew Assignment: Station a dedicated driver and an alert safety observer inside the towboat.
Step 3 - Equipment Check: Examine the tow rope and bridle hardware for strand fraying and knots.
Step 4 - Emergency Drill: Practice rapid engine cutoffs and recovery approaches during a simulated skier fall.

pamphlet_excerpts: Deepwater Starting Posture: Keep knees bent deeply against chest while holding ski tips above the water.
Arms Straight Technique: Allow boat pull to draw body upward without prematurely pulling arms into chest.
Wake Crossing Angle: Attack wake crests at a sharp diagonal angle while keeping knees flexed.
Handle Release Procedure: Drop the tow handle cleanly and coast smoothly until momentum dissipates in water.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Deepwater Setup: Crouch in deep water with ski tips protruding above surface between towline bridle.
Step 2 - Planing Phase: Let the boat pull you upright into a balanced athletic stance upon acceleration.
Step 3 - Wake Traversal: Lean outward and cut across both wakes diagonally with bent knees absorbing chop.
Step 4 - Controlled Dismount: Release the tow handle, sink into water hips-first, and protect your head.
